sections.title: Weapon and ammunition
paragraphs: The M4A1 is an assault rifle using 5.56×45 mm ammunition. The community database lists single and automatic fire, with a reference magazine of 30 rounds. Those catalogue values are not a verified Operations build: attachments and mode-specific balancing can change the result.

sections.title: Prepare an Operations loadout
paragraphs: Garena’s guide describes buying or exchanging battle supplies and moving equipment from Stash into Loadout. Check M4A1 availability and requirements in your own client. Do not use a Warfare level-unlock guide as proof of the Operations acquisition route.

sections.title: Ammunition is part of the build
paragraphs: The database lists M995, M855A1, M855, FMJ and RRLP as compatible 5.56×45 mm choices. Compatibility is not a recommendation to buy the most expensive round. Compare the client’s penetration, damage and cost information against the raid you are preparing for.

sections.title: Build a repeatable range test
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: save a plain M4A1 build, choose one target distance, and fire the same-length burst before changing a single attachment. Record ammunition, sight and magazine along with the result. Prefer a configuration you can control consistently over a copied popularity ranking.

sections.title: Codes, server and patch
paragraphs: Garena explicitly warns that its share codes are for the Garena version. This dossier does not certify any imported build, recoil pattern or time-to-kill figure. Read the Operations label and inspect the final in-game configuration before buying parts; screenshots can outlive the patch they depict.

sections.title: AKM identity
paragraphs: The AKM is a 7.62×39 mm assault rifle. Community reference data lists single and automatic fire and a 30-round magazine. It is not interchangeable with every weapon bearing an AK name: ammunition family, compatible attachments and imported codes need the exact model.

sections.title: Choose compatible rounds
paragraphs: Listed ammunition includes AP, BP, PS, T45M and LP in 7.62×39 mm. The names identify different rounds rather than cosmetic skins. The weapon page mixes mode references, so its headline damage and fire-rate table is not reproduced here as confirmed current Operations performance.

sections.title: Prepare the whole kit
paragraphs: Use the Stash and Loadout screens to check weapon, magazines, spare ammunition and medical supplies together. The official starter guide explains the Supply Station and progression-dependent stock. Specific AKM offers, barter requirements and prices must be read in the installed regional client.

sections.title: Control before expense
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: compare short bursts against sustained fire at the same distance, then inspect where missed rounds land. Change only one recoil-related attachment per comparison. Keep a note of the final weapon name and ammunition so a later session can reproduce the test instead of merely copying a screenshot.

sections.title: Do not merge Warfare rules
paragraphs: An Operations loadout must be assessed in Operations. A Warfare class restriction or unlock level is not automatically valid here. No current-market budget, guaranteed armor break or universal best build is claimed. Check version and server labels before importing community codes.

sections.title: SMG identity
paragraphs: The MP5 is a 9×19 mm submachine gun. The community database lists single, burst and automatic fire, plus a 30-round reference magazine. It is a different platform from the SMG-45 or P90; do not transfer an ammunition list just because all three belong to the SMG family.

sections.title: Compatible ammunition
paragraphs: The reference lists PBP, AP6.3, Pst, PSO and RIP as 9×19 mm options. Use the client to inspect each round’s actual attributes. A compatible cartridge does not imply equal effect against armor; build selection should consider the ammunition you can carry, not only the gun image.

sections.title: Loadout checks
paragraphs: Check the exact MP5 listing in the Supply Station or your existing Stash, then inspect ammunition compatibility before deployment. Official Operations guidance covers equipment preparation and exchange systems; it does not establish a permanent MP5 price or universally available starter reward.

sections.title: Practice a close-range route
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: set a short target route with a corner and cover. Compare aimed fire with hip fire while recording which attachments changed. Repeat after a reload so the test includes recovery time, and leave room in the plan to disengage instead of treating every close encounter as a required fight.

sections.title: Reference limits
paragraphs: The database’s build list includes Warfare entries. Its numerical table has not been verified for your current PC Operations build, so no universal damage or range claim is made. Region-specific share codes and patch changes should be checked in the Gunsmith before purchasing a complete kit.
